Intermediate Backend Engineer, Security Factory: Code Security

An overview of this role

As an Intermediate Backend Engineer on GitLab's Security Factory: Code Security team, you'll help developers find and fix security issues in the code they write and the open source components they depend on.

Your work connects dependency analysis, vulnerability detection, and automated remediation. You'll build parsing that tells the security analysis engine which libraries and frameworks a project uses, extend a service that turns security advisories into dependency update merge requests, and develop hybrid analyzers that combine rule-based detection with artificial intelligence (AI) reasoning. You'll help evaluate how well those analyzers find real vulnerabilities and expand coverage of libraries, frameworks, and AI agent tooling.

We use AI-assisted development tools in our daily work and expect you to use them effectively and with good judgment.

What you’ll do

  • Develop secure, well-tested, performant parsing for dependency manifests, lockfiles, and software bills of materials (SBOMs). Extend support for new package ecosystems and formats in the analysis engine and remediation service.
  • Build and apply analyzers that combine deterministic analysis with AI-driven analysis, working with the team's technical leadership. Review their results and measure false positives and missed findings against benchmark applications with known vulnerabilities.
  • Create detection rules mapped to Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) and the test fixtures that prove they work.
  • Contribute to packaging analyzers for continuous integration (CI) jobs, AI agent workflows, and command-line tools, reporting findings in GitLab's standard security report formats.
  • Extend the automated remediation service, from running dependency updates in a sandbox to opening merge requests.
  • Solve technical problems of moderate scope and complexity. Identify technical debt that slows the team down, and propose and implement improvements.
  • Write maintainable code that meets our internal standards, and help maintain those standards through code review.
  • Participate in on-call rotations to troubleshoot product operations, security operations, and urgent engineering issues.

What you’ll bring

  • Experience using AI or large language model (LLM) tools to generate or evaluate technical content, with the judgment to know when output is trustworthy and when it isn't.
  • Solid professional experience writing and testing production code in a systems language, particularly Go and/or Rust. We use both, plus Ruby for remediation and Python for some analyzers, and value a willingness to work across them.
  • A willingness to learn how vulnerabilities arise in code and the software supply chain, explore common vulnerability classes such as the Open Worldwide Application Security Project (OWASP) Top 10 and CWE, and apply static analysis to detect them. Deep expertise isn't required, and we'll help you develop it.
  • The ability to organize your work and follow through on tasks independently in a remote, largely asynchronous environment.
  • The ability to communicate clearly and concisely about technical problems and propose iterative solutions.
  • Helpful, but not required: experience with containerized workflows and continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD), or a willingness to learn them; package managers and dependency tooling such as npm, Maven, pip, Bundler, or Cargo; web or mobile frameworks; parsing, abstract syntax trees (ASTs), program analysis, or detection rules; or evaluating AI-driven detection against labeled data. We use Docker heavily.

About the team

The Security Factory: Code Security team builds GitLab's code-level security scanning capabilities, spanning static application security testing (SAST) and dependency scanning.

We work closely with the Static Analysis team on GitLab's SAST engines, with Composition Analysis on the broader software supply chain, and with other groups across the Sec section. We rely heavily on asynchronous work across time zones.

 

How GitLab Supports Full-Time Employees

  • Benefits to support your health, finances, and well-being
  • Flexible Paid Time Off 
  • Team Member Resource Groups
  • Equity Compensation & Employee Stock Purchase Plan
  • Growth and Development Fund
  • Parental Leave 

Please note that we welcome interest from candidates with varying levels of experience; many successful candidates do not meet every single requirement. Additionally, studies have shown that people from underrepresented groups are less likely to apply to a job unless they meet every single qualification. If you're excited about this role, please apply and allow our recruiters to assess your application.

Country Hiring Guidelines: GitLab hires new team members in countries around the world. All of our roles are remote, however some roles may carry specific location-based eligibility requirements. Our Talent Acquisition team can help answer any questions about location after starting the recruiting process.  

Privacy Policy: Please review our Recruitment Privacy Policy. Your privacy is important to us.

An overview of this role

As an Intermediate Backend Engineer on GitLab's Cells Infrastructure team, you'll help build the architecture that lets GitLab.com scale horizontally. Cells splits GitLab.com into independent units, each with its own application and data stack, behind a shared routing layer.

You'll build the services and application changes that make Cells work: the control plane that tracks cells and organizations, the routing logic that sends each request to the right cell, and the changes inside the GitLab application that keep data unique and consistent across cells. Your work will directly support moving customer organizations onto Cells, one of GitLab's most important scaling initiatives.

You'll work across Go, Ruby on Rails, and TypeScript.

What you’ll do

  • Design, build, and maintain the Cells control plane, a Go service using gRPC (remote procedure calls) and backed by Cloud Spanner that tracks cells, organizations, and globally unique resources.
  • Extend the global routing layer, written in TypeScript on Cloudflare Workers, so requests reach the right cell. This includes classifying requests by path, namespace, and token, and supporting more protocols and services.
  • Make changes in the GitLab Rails application so it works across multiple cells: claiming globally unique resources, propagating organization context, and keeping cell-local data consistent.
  • Design application programming interfaces (APIs) and data models with correctness, idempotency, and backward compatibility in mind, so changes can roll out safely across a fleet of cells.
  • Write thorough automated tests, including unit, integration, and end-to-end tests, and improve test coverage and reliability across the services we own.
  • Instrument your services with OpenTelemetry for metrics, logs, and distributed tracing. Help define service level objectives (SLOs) and take part in on-call for the services you build.
  • Work with product teams to make their features cell-compatible, and review their changes for Cells correctness.
  • Write clear design documents, architecture decision records, and documentation, and take part in code review as both author and reviewer.

What you’ll bring

  • Professional experience building and running backend services in production, including monitoring, debugging, and incident response. You've instrumented services with OpenTelemetry and used distributed tracing to debug requests across service boundaries.
  • Proficiency in Go, or strong experience in another backend language and willingness to work in Go daily.
  • Experience with Ruby on Rails and TypeScript, or the willingness to become productive in both. Our control plane is written in Go, the GitLab application in Rails, and our edge routing layer in TypeScript.
  • Experience designing APIs using gRPC or Representational State Transfer (REST), and working with relational or distributed databases, including schema design, transactions, and migrations.
  • A strong understanding of distributed-systems fundamentals, such as consistency, idempotency, concurrency, retries, and failure handling.
  • Solid grounding in engineering best practices: test-driven development, small iterative merge requests, thorough code review, feature flags for safe rollouts, and observable, well-documented code.
  • Experience working effectively in distributed, all-remote teams: you default to asynchronous, written-first communication, document decisions in issues and merge requests, hand off work cleanly across time zones, and stay transparent about progress and blockers.
  • If you've worked with Cloud Spanner, Cloudflare Workers, Kubernetes, multi-tenant or sharded architectures, or contributed to GitLab, that's a plus, not a requirement.

About the team

The Cells Infrastructure team is part of GitLab's Scale & Architecture organization, which builds and operates the core services that let GitLab.com grow. Every team in the organization owns its services end to end, from design through on-call.

Beyond the control plane and routing services you'll help build, we're responsible for:

  • Provisioning cells across Amazon Web Services (AWS) and Google Cloud.
  • Ring-based deployments that keep the fleet in step with GitLab's release cadence.
  • SLOs, alerting, and on-call for the platform.
  • The infrastructure for moving customer organizations between cells.

Our team mixes Backend Engineers and Site Reliability Engineers who work side by side on the same services. We work closely with delivery, database, migration, and product teams across GitLab. Feature teams own how their services behave on the Cells platform.

We're an all-remote, asynchronous team. We make decisions in GitLab issues, use directly responsible individuals (DRIs) to own technical direction, demo our work weekly, and use artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted workflows every day.

  • Team Member Resource Groups

At GoDaddy the future of work looks different for each team. Some teams work in the office full-time; others have a hybrid arrangement (they work remotely some days and in the office some days) and some work entirely remotely.​

This is a remote position, so you’ll be working remotely from your home. You may occasionally visit a GoDaddy office to meet with your team for events or meetings.  

Join Our Team...
GoDaddy's Network Security Engineering and Operations team is looking for a Network Security Automation Engineer to build and run the software that manages network security at scale. Are you equally comfortable reading a firewall rule base and a CI pipeline?
In this role you'll own the internal APIs and risk engine behind our network policy management, automate our operational workflows, and find the problems nobody has filed a ticket for! Because this tooling holds privileged access to the network, the role requires real security judgment, not just software skills.

What you'll get to do...

  • Own and extend the internal APIs and services that drive network security policy management, including our risk calculation engine
  • Automate operational workflows from request intake and validation through change execution, evidence capture and reporting
  • Write, test and maintain production code, partnering with our SRE team on deployment, monitoring and release
  • Integrate with firewalls, segmentation platforms, asset sources, ticketing and network detection tooling through their APIs
  • Help stand up network detection and response capability and automate detection validation across NDR, IDS and IPS

Your experience should include...

  • 3+ years in network security, network engineering, infrastructure automation or a platform/tooling role, with tools and services you've built and shipped
  • Strong Python proficiency, with tested, maintainable production code. Demonstrated network security depth: firewall policy, segmentation, ACLs and routing across devices, hosts and cloud
  • Experience with Git and CI/CD, and enough understanding of containerized deployment to work effectively with SRE teams
  • Fluency with REST APIs, TLS and certificates, and secure coding practices. Ability to take a loosely defined problem, propose an approach and deliver it independently
  • Experience using AI tools to solve real engineering problems, with the judgment to know when the output is wrong

You might also have...

  • Experience with Juniper SRX, Palo Alto Networks, Tufin or Illumio
  • Infrastructure-as-code experience with Terraform, CloudFormation or Kubernetes - AWS networking, IAM and serverless automation experience
  • Experience automating detections on NDR, IDS or IPS platforms.
  • Experience working with flow data, firewall and DNS logs, or SIEM platforms

We encourage you to apply even if your experience or skillset doesn’t align perfectly with every requirement. We value a wide range of backgrounds and transferable skills, and we are excited to support learning and growth.

We've got your back... We offer a range of total rewards that may include paid time off, retirement savings (e.g., 401k, pension schemes), bonus/incentive eligibility, equity grants, participation in our employee stock purchase plan, competitive health benefits, and other family-friendly benefits including parental leave. GoDaddy’s benefits vary based on individual role and location and can be reviewed in more detail during the interview process.

Zscaler (NASDAQ: ZS) accelerates digital transformation so customers can be more agile, efficient, resilient, and secure. The Zscaler Zero Trust Exchange platform protects thousands of customers from cyberattacks and data loss by securely connecting users, devices, and applications in any location. Distributed across 200+ public data centers globally and thousands of private sites at the edge, the SASE-based Zero Trust Exchange is the world’s largest in-line cloud security platform.

We believe the future of work is Human + AI and are building an AI-native enterprise where human potential is amplified by machine intelligence to solve the world’s hardest security challenges. Driven by deep customer obsession, we are committed to the mission, outcome, and to each other. We bring these commitments to life through three core behaviors: ownership and collaboration, trust through outcomes and impact, and a challenge culture with ongoing feedback. Ready to make an impact at the company pioneering security transformation in the AI era? Join us at Zscaler.

Role

We are looking for a Software Development Engineer to join our team. This is a hybrid role based in Hyderabad, reporting to the Director of Software Engineering. You will join the Engineering team that built the world’s largest cloud security platform from the ground up. As a leader in our multitenant architecture, you will bring your vision and passion to help organizations worldwide harness speed and agility with a cloud-first strategy.

What you’ll do (Role Expectations)

  • Understand how to build and operate high scale systems
  • Provide service and product wide architectural guidance, and drive impactful technical decisions
  • Establish and enforce best practices for coding, testing, observability, and CI/CD pipelines to maintain high-quality, production-ready services
  • Drive cross-team collaboration and lead initiatives in performance optimization, reliability improvements, and adoption of new technologies/tools to accelerate feature velocity

Who You Are (Success Profile)

  • You thrive in ambiguity. You're comfortable building the path as you walk it. You thrive in a dynamic environment, seeing ambiguity not as a hindrance, but as the raw material to build something meaningful.
  • You act like an owner. Your passion for the mission fuels your bias for action. You operate with integrity because you genuinely care about the outcome. True ownership involves leveraging dynamic range: the ability to navigate seamlessly between high-level strategy and hands-on execution.
  • You are a problem-solver. You love running towards the challenges because you are laser-focused on finding the solution, knowing that solving the hard problems delivers the biggest impact.
  • You are a high-trust collaborator. You are ambitious for the team, not just yourself. You embrace our challenge culture by giving and receiving ongoing feedback—knowing that candor delivered with clarity and respect is the truest form of teamwork and the fastest way to earn trust.
  • You are a learner. You have a true growth mindset and are obsessed with your own development, actively seeking feedback to become a better partner and a stronger teammate. You love what you do and you do it with purpose.

What We’re Looking for (Minimum Qualifications)

  • Foundational understanding of AI/ML technologies and experience leveraging, securing, or positioning AI-driven solutions to optimize outcomes within your functional domain and experience with agentic AI systems and orchestration workflows
  • 2+ years of experience in Java coding in a highly distributed and enterprise-scale environment
  • Working knowledge of cloud infrastructure services on AWS or Azure
  • Strong experience with distributed systems and microservices architecture
  • Strong database knowledge of SQL constructs and data modeling
  • Strong experience with Identity governance and administration, Access Management

What Will Make You Stand Out (Preferred Qualifications)

  • Experience leveraging AI coding assistants, automated code review tooling, or LLM-assisted development workflows to optimize software architecture and accelerate delivery cycles
  • Experience building reliable data tiers using Postgres, Redis, Terraform, Ansible, graph databases like Neo4j or AWS Neptune, and developing GraphQL APIs
  • Knowledge of identity and access management systems (Okta, SAML, OAuth), test automation, Python programming, and designing fault-tolerant distributed systems for networking or cloud security products

Elastic, the Search AI Company, enables everyone to find the answers they need in real time, using all their data, at scale — unleashing the potential of businesses and people. The Elastic Search AI Platform, used by more than 50% of the Fortune 500, brings together the precision of search and the intelligence of AI to enable everyone to accelerate the results that matter. By taking advantage of all structured and unstructured data — securing and protecting private information more effectively — Elastic’s complete, cloud-based solutions for search, security, and observability help organizations deliver on the promise of AI.

What is The Role

Elastic, makers of the hugely popular open source products Elasticsearch, Kibana, Logstash, and Beats, is growing very fast and so is our marketing team. As a key member of the Marketing AI, Operations and Automation team, you will play a hands-on, critical role in designing and building the automation infrastructure that powers marketing at scale. From connecting systems via APIs and webhooks to calling AI models for reasoning within live workflows, you will be the technical builder behind how marketing teams work smarter and move faster.

Elastic is looking for a flexible and adaptable person with the ability to manage a variety of integration and automation challenges across a modern marketing tech stack. This is an ideal position for a self-motivated individual who has hands-on experience with no-code platforms and system integrations, is comfortable working directly with APIs and LLMs, and has the ability to work in a fast-paced, distributed environment.

What You Will Be Doing

  • Design and build automated marketing workflows using no-code and low-code platforms, connecting tools across the marketing tech stack so data flows reliably between systems without manual intervention.
  • Integrate marketing platforms, AI content tools, and third-party services via APIs and webhooks, handling authentication, error states, and data formatting across each connection.
  • Work with AI models and generative AI platforms to build structured, repeatable workflows that produce consistent outputs at scale, configuring prompts and agent behaviour at the system level.
  • Call LLM APIs to trigger AI reasoning within workflows, constructing prompts programmatically, handling model responses, and routing outputs back to connected systems
  • Gather requirements from marketing teams across functions and translate them into workflow specifications, identifying opportunities for reuse and cross-team impact over single-team solutions.
  • Own the reliability and maintainability of the workflows you build, writing documentation clear enough for non-technical stakeholders to understand what runs, why, and how.
  • Evaluate new tools and integration patterns as the marketing tech stack evolves, recommending additions based on technical fit and organisational need.
  • Collaborate with operations, regional marketing, content, demand generation, and other marketing teams to understand where automation removes friction and build accordingly.

What You Bring

  • 4+ years in marketing operations, marketing technology engineering, or a closely adjacent technical role focused on integrations and automation.
  • Hands-on experience building multi-step workflows using no-code or low-code platforms such as Workfront Fusion, Zapier, Make, or n8n in a production environment.
  • Practical experience working with APIs and webhooks: constructing authenticated requests, reading API documentation, handling errors, and passing data between systems reliably.
  • Experience connecting marketing platforms (Workfront, Marketo, Google Workspace, or similar) to external tools and services through system-level integrations.
  • Experience working with at least one AI model or generative AI platform in a workflow or integration context, including configuring system-level prompts and handling structured outputs.
  • Experience calling LLM APIs to trigger AI reasoning within a workflow, including constructing prompts programmatically, handling responses, and routing outputs back to connected systems.
  • Ability to gather requirements from non-technical stakeholders and convert them into buildable workflow specifications.
  • Strong written documentation habits, with the ability to make complex automation logic understandable to others.
  • Experience working across globally distributed teams spanning multiple time zones.
  • Preferred experience with Workfront, Zapier, Marketo, Adobe Fusion, Google Suite.

Bonus Points

  • Google Apps Script, JavaScript, or Python for cases where no-code tools reach their limits.

Additional Information - We Take Care of Our People

As a distributed company, diversity drives our identity. Whether you’re looking to launch a new career or grow an existing one, Elastic is the type of company where you can balance great work with great life. Your age is only a number. It doesn’t matter if you’re just out of college or your children are; we need you for what you can do.

About Sarvam Sarvam is building the bedrock of Sovereign AI for India. The company is developing India's full-stack sovereign AI platform, building across research, models, infrastructure and applications with a singular focus on making AI genuinely work for India. Sarvam works with leading enterprises and public institutions and is backed by Lightspeed, Peak XV and Khosla Ventures. Sarvam partners with India's leading brands, including Tata Capital, SBI Life, CRED, IDFC and LIC. About the role Sarvam's model APIs (ASR, TTS, Vision, LLM, Translate) are how developers and enterprises ship products on our foundation models. The platform handles tens of millions of API calls every day, over HTTP and WebSockets, with metering, billing, prepaid wallets and rate-limiting all part of the same stack. We are hiring a Software Engineer to own major parts of this platform end to end, working closely with the Staff Engineer who leads its architecture. You will take an area such as speech to text pipeline,or text to speech pipeline, and be accountable for its reliability, performance and end-to-end latencies. This role is for someone who is obsessed with latencies, optimizes services and network paths to shave off milliseconds, ships fast, reasons from first principles, and treats AI as the default way to get engineering work done. What you will do Own a platform area end to end • Own one or more major parts of the platform, such as the WebSocket streaming layer, a speech recognition pipeline, or text to speech pipeline: build, operate and improve them. • Turn loosely defined goals into RFCs, milestones and shipped results, and write down the decisions and trade-offs. • Be accountable after launch: on-call, incident response, root-cause analysis and follow-through on fixes. • Make the call when a decision is needed, and own the outcome. • Obsessed with latencies, dissecting existing services to understand the system, and tuning the right knobs to optimize performance. • Bring services across without regressions in customer-facing APIs, latency or reliability. Build real-time and model-serving pipelines • Build and operate streaming infrastructure: WebSocket connections, long-lived sessions queue-based batch processing, backpressure and low-latency model invocation. • Engineer audio pipelines: TTS chunking around model context limits, sample-rate conversion and format encoding, and VAD-based silence detection for ASR. • Hold your services to sub-100ms latency SLOs in a multi-tenant environment, and know where every millisecond goes. Think in systems and from first principles • Reasons from constraints: latency budgets per hop, throughput, cost per request, failure modes and tenant isolation. • Use back-of-the-envelope estimates to decide what to build, what to optimize and what to leave alone. • Prefer simple designs you can fully explain over clever ones you cannot. • Build in observability from day one: logging, metrics and tracing that let anyone debug production quickly. Raise the bar for the team • Strengthen the integration testing harness so the team can ship fast without breaking customer-facing APIs. • Partner with the Inference and MLOps teams on making model serving fast, reliable and operable. • Mentor junior engineers through RFC reviews, code review and pairing. • Practice design-first, documentation-first engineering: RFCs before code, no tribal knowledge. What we are looking for • 4–6 years of building and operating production backend systems. • At least one service you owned end to end under real load, including what broke and what you changed. • Strong distributed-systems fundamentals: concurrency, networking, queues, caching, consistency and failure modes. • Experience with low-latency or high-throughput services, and comfort reasoning about p95 and p99 latency. • Solid fundamentals with a relational database and a cache, such as PostgreSQL and Redis: schema design, query performance and caching strategy. • Fluency in at least one backend language and willingness to work in both Python and Golang. • Experience running services with containers, CI/CD and production monitoring. • Daily, hands-on use of AI tools in your engineering workflow, with concrete examples of what you automated or sped up. • A bias for action: fast on reversible decisions, careful on irreversible ones. • Clear writing, especially RFCs and design docs that others can act on. Good to have (not required) • Voice AI or real-time audio experience: WebSockets, WebRTC, streaming ASR or TTS, or audio processing with FFmpeg or pyav, codecs, sample rates and VAD. • Production experience in Go, or in Python with FastAPI. • Experience serving LLM, ASR, TTS or vision models in production. • Experience building metering, billing, wallet or payments infrastructure. • Running services on Kubernetes in production. • Time at an early- or growth-stage startup. Why Sarvam • A fast-moving, high talent-density team building full-stack AI for India, with real population-scale impact. • Researchers, engineers, builders and business leaders who move fast and hold each other to a very high bar. • High ownership and high impact from day one. • AI-first in everything, from how we build and ship to how we think about problems
